newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Little impact in S.Korea from all-out strike call.
newsitem.headline: Little impact in S.Korea from all-out strike call.

text.p: All-out strikes called by South Korea's largest umbrella union group had only a token impact on Tuesday, with buses and commuter trains running normally, witnesses said.

The Federation of Korean Trade Unions, with 1.2 million members, ordered two-day stoppages throughout the nation to protest azgainst at a controversial labour law rammed through parliament on December 26 allowing companies to lay off workers.
Seoul citizens said the only difference on Tuesday morning was that there were fewer taxis on the street as many drivers responded to the strike call.
The legislation sparked a wave of stoppages for almost three weeks that has crippled key industries in export-oriented South Korea. But many workers returned to factories, working intermittently.
Union leaders said the impact of strikes would be serious on Wednesday when telecommunications workers and subway and bus drivers were due to join.
A militant union body has also called for all-out strikes, including a public-sector shutout, from Wednesday unless the government repeals the labour law by midnight Tuesday.
The group, the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, claims 500,000 members.
Officials of the Seoul city government said they had worked out steps to ease impact from any public sector stoppages.

But subway strikes staged last year by the confederation left little impact on services. A spokesman of the Seoul Metropolitan Rapid Transit said he was confident trains would run normally with non-union drivers.
Union members at banks are due to stage a four-hour strike on Tuesday afternoon but their representatives said tellers would continue serving customers.
